name: SR-22 filing duration by US state — how long you must carry the certificate, quoted from the state DMV
description: An SR-22 (or the higher-limit FR-44 some states substitute after a DUI) is a certificate an insurer files with the state proving a driver carries the mandated coverage, and states differ both in how long the filing must run — commonly two to five years — and in what restarts the clock, such as a lapse in coverage or a new conviction. Every existing comparison of this figure is an insurance agency's marketing page, none of which cite the state DMV statute or page a figure is drawn from, so a reader has no way to check a number against its source. Each record is one state, with the required filing duration, what starts the clock (conviction date, reinstatement date, or judgment date), which suspension the duration applies to, what happens if coverage lapses during that period, and the DMV page or statute it comes from, backed by a verbatim quote. A state whose own agency states more than one duration — Missouri sets two years after an accident judgment and three after a mandatory-insurance suspension — gets one record per duration rather than a single averaged answer. Answers 'how long do I need an SR-22' and 'when does my SR-22 requirement end'.

records.source_citation: Section 10: Financial Responsibility, Insurance Requirements, and Collisions
records.source_quote: You can get your driver’s license back during the last three years of the suspension if you provide a California Insurance Proof Certificate (SR 22/SR 1P) and maintain it during the three-year period.

records.requirement_trigger: reinstatement of driving privileges after the effective date of a suspension under the Financial Responsibility Act
records.lapse_consequence: Your driver license will be suspended for that reason alone
records.source_quote: Include an SR22 (future proof of automobile liability insurance from your insurance company) and maintain it continuously for three years following restoration of your driving privileges;

records.clock_start: the date you were eligible to reinstate
records.requirement_trigger: you were suspended for False Insurance or Mandatory Insurance
records.source_quote: If you were suspended for False Insurance or Mandatory Insurance, you must maintain insurance on file with the Driver License Bureau for three years from the date you were eligible to reinstate.

records.clock_start: the date of reinstatement of their driving privilege
records.requirement_trigger: a DUI conviction that occurred after October 1, 2007
records.source_quote: The customer must maintain the FR-44 form for three years from the date of reinstatement of their driving privilege.

records.requirement_trigger: convicted of a second or more 'No Insurance' citation
records.lapse_consequence: this will result in the cancellation of your driver's license
records.source_quote: Driver must maintain an SR-22/SR-22A "Non-Owners" Insurance Policy for 3 years from the conviction date. You will prepay in full each 6-months.

records.requirement_trigger: required to file proof of financial responsibility by Illinois law
records.source_quote: The SR-22 Certificate must be maintained for 36 months (three years).

records.clock_start: the starting date of the suspension
records.requirement_trigger: you were suspended for a Motor Vehicle Accident Judgment (Missouri or Out-of-State)
records.source_quote: If you were suspended for a Motor Vehicle Accident Judgment (Missouri or Out-of-State), you must maintain insurance on file with the Driver License Bureau for two years from the starting date of the suspension.

records.clock_start: upon reinstatement of your Nevada driver's license
records.requirement_trigger: your issue relates DUI, revocation, accident, lapse of SR-22, lapse of insurance
records.lapse_consequence: the suspension of your license and will restart the three-year requirement
records.source_quote: Keep It for 3 Years Failure to maintain continuous SR-22 coverage will result in the suspension of your license and will restart the three-year requirement. The three-year SR-22 requirement begins upon reinstatement of your Nevada driver's license. Do not obtain an SR-22 before reinstatement, as it will not count toward the requirement.

records.clock_start: the date of your most recent conviction, or the date that a judgement has been rendered against you
records.requirement_trigger: Driving While Intoxicated, Drug Offenses, Driving While License Invalid, and multiple convictions for No Motor Vehicle Liability Insurance
records.lapse_consequence: your driver license and/or driving privilege would be re-suspended and a new SR-22 and a $100 reinstatement fee would be required to reinstate your driver license
records.source_quote: You must maintain a valid SR-22 for two years from the date of your most recent conviction, or the date that a judgement has been rendered against you.

records.requirement_trigger: the motor vehicle is subsequently found to be uninsured
records.source_quote: These items are suspended until the person: Pays a $600 non-compliance fee Furnishes and maintains proof of financial responsibility (form SR-22) for three years Pays a reinstatement fee, if applicable

records.clock_start: the date you're eligible to reinstate your license
records.requirement_trigger: Been convicted of, or forfeited bail for, certain offenses. Failed to pay judgments. Driven or owned a vehicle involved in an accident.
records.source_quote: How long do I have to provide proof of financial responsibility? In most cases, 3 years from the date you're eligible to reinstate your license.
